sentences.text: Ibirania is a genus of dwarf saltasaurine titanosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Southeast Brazil.
This animal ranks among the smallest known sauropods, with a size comparable to Magyarosaurus.
Scientists estimate the creature reached a length of exactly 5.7 meters.
The name Ibirania means "tree wanderer," combining the discovery location Ibirá with the Greek word for wanderer.
Fossilized parasites were found preserved inside the vascular canals of an Ibirania bone lesion, representing the first such report in a dinosaur.
CT scans revealed that Ibirania possessed highly pneumatized vertebrae with a bird-like air sac system.
A partial fibula shows evidence of acute osteomyelitis, an infection that caused periosteal remodeling.
Ibirania is classified as a derived member of the Saltasaurinae, a clade containing some of the smallest titanosaurs.
Phylogenetic analysis places Ibirania as the sister taxon to the clade formed by the Patagonian saltasaurines Bonatitan and Rocasaurus.
Ibirania lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 86 and 75 million years ago.
The animal coexisted with the abelisaurid theropod Thanos simonattoi, a large unnamed probable megaraptoran, and an indeterminate notosuchian.
